overview: Surah Al-Ikhlas (The Sincerity / Purity of Faith) is the 112th chapter of the Holy Quran, revealed in Makkah and consisting of 4 short verses in Juz 30. Although one of the briefest chapters in the Quran, it offers the clearest and most concise definition of Islamic monotheism (tawhid).

The surah affirms four foundational truths about Allah: He is One and Unique (Ahad); He is As-Samad—the Eternal Refuge upon Whom all creation depends while He depends on none; He neither begets nor was begotten; and there is nothing comparable to Him in any respect.

Because the Quran's message revolves around three broad domains—tawhid (knowledge of Allah), prophetic narratives, and practical laws—scholars explain that Surah Al-Ikhlas encapsulates the domain of tawhid in its purest form. Together with Surah Al-Falaq and Surah An-Nas, it is widely recited in daily prayers and morning and evening remembrances.
mainThemes: Absolute oneness and uniqueness of Allah (Ahad).
Allah as As-Samad—self-sufficient, eternal, and the refuge of all creation.
Rejection of any lineage, partner, or likeness attributed to God.

virtues.text: The Prophet ﷺ stated that Surah Al-Ikhlas ('Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad') is equivalent in reward to one-third of the Quran.
Every night when the Prophet ﷺ went to bed, he would cup his hands together, blow into them, recite Surah Al-Ikhlas, Surah Al-Falaq, and Surah An-Nas, and wipe over his body three times.

faqs.question: How many verses are in Surah Al-Ikhlas?
faqs.answer: Surah Al-Ikhlas has 4 verses (ayahs) and is located in Juz 30.

faqs.question: Why is Surah Al-Ikhlas equal to one-third of the Quran?
faqs.answer: Authentic narrations in Sahih al-Bukhari (5013) and Sahih Muslim (811) affirm that Surah Al-Ikhlas equals one-third of the Quran, as it completely summarizes tawhid—one of the three core themes of the Quran alongside laws and stories.

faqs.question: What does As-Samad mean in Surah Al-Ikhlas?
faqs.answer: As-Samad means the Eternal, Self-Sufficient Master and Refuge upon Whom all creation depends for every need, while He needs nothing.

faqs.question: Is Surah Al-Ikhlas Makki or Madani?
faqs.answer: Surah Al-Ikhlas is a Makki surah, revealed in Makkah.

relatedSurahs.reason: Surah Al-Falaq is recited alongside Al-Ikhlas before sleep and in daily adhkar.
Surah An-Nas completes the trio of closing surahs (the Quls).
Surah Al-Fatihah opens the Quran with praise and tawhid.
